claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have a child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 13 years old.

Now I need to ask you some questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, this may affect your eligibility, but there are some circumstances where you can still claim Child Benefit while living outside the UK.

**Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you or your partner a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not comfortable sharing exactly which country right now, but no - neither myself nor my partner work for the government or armed forces. We're just regular people living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, thank you for clarifying.

Based on the information you've provided, let me assess your situation:

- You have a 13-year-old son, Alex
- You live abroad (outside the UK)
- You are not a Crown servant or in the armed forces

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. There are exceptions for people living in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant, but since neither of those apply to your situation, this affects your eligibility.

**Just to complete my assessment: Does Alex live with you abroad, or does he live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives back in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

**Can you tell me who Alex is currently living with in the UK? For example, is he living with another parent, a relative, or someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his other parent - my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. 

**One final question: Are you making any financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep - such as paying for clothes, food, pocket money, maintenance payments, or contributing to his accommodation costs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I send money regularly for things like his clothes, school expenses, that sort of thing - about £26 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now assess your eligibility for Child Benefit.

Based on what you've told me:
- Alex is 13 years old and lives in the UK with his other parent (your ex-partner)
- You live abroad (not in the UK)
- You are not a Crown servant
- You contribute approximately £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. The exceptions are for people living in certain specific countries or Crown servants, neither of which apply to your situation.

Additionally, since Alex lives with his other parent in the UK, that parent would typically be the one eligible to claim Child Benefit, as they are the one living with Alex. Only one person can get Child Benefit for a child.

While you are contributing financially to Alex's upkeep, the requirement to live in the UK (unless you fall under specific exceptions) means you would not be eligible for Child Benefit in your current circumstances.

Alex's other parent, who lives with him in the UK, would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit if they haven't already done so.
